questions.prompt:
A paper reports faster inference on one hardware setup but its introduction discusses broad efficiency goals.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Separate the paper's central claim from background, implementation details and speculative implications. A useful reading note states what changed, compared with what baseline, and under which conditions.

Research claims should match the scope of the evidence.
keyPoints: Research claims should match the scope of the evidence.
Separate the paper's central claim from background, implementation details and speculative implications.

questions.prompt:
A method assumes access to labeled target-domain examples unavailable in the intended deployment.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Inspect data selection, training conditions and evaluation procedures before interpreting headline results. Hidden assumptions can determine whether a method transfers to another workload.

Applicability depends on the method's actual assumptions.
keyPoints: Applicability depends on the method's actual assumptions.
Inspect data selection, training conditions and evaluation procedures before interpreting headline results.

questions.prompt:
A team asks whether retrieval improves answers on documents with recent policy changes compared with the same model without retrieval.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A research question should specify a variable, outcome and comparison that could contradict the hypothesis. Narrow questions make resource needs and success criteria clearer.

A useful hypothesis can be contradicted by a specified observation.
keyPoints: A useful hypothesis can be contradicted by a specified observation.
A research question should specify a variable, outcome and comparison that could contradict the hypothesis.

questions.prompt:
Several summaries repeat the same original experiment, creating an illusion of independent support.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Group related work by problem, assumptions and method rather than collecting titles alone. Track primary sources and distinguish reproduced findings from secondary summaries.

Multiple summaries of one study are not independent evidence.
keyPoints: Multiple summaries of one study are not independent evidence.
Group related work by problem, assumptions and method rather than collecting titles alone.

questions.prompt:
A new retriever is tuned extensively while the baseline uses an unsuitable default configuration.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Baselines should be relevant, competently configured and evaluated under comparable conditions. An artificially weak baseline exaggerates the apparent contribution.

Baseline quality affects the credibility of reported gains.
keyPoints: Baseline quality affects the credibility of reported gains.
Baselines should be relevant, competently configured and evaluated under comparable conditions.

questions.prompt:
A model update changes architecture, dataset and training duration together.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Change the intended factor while holding other influential conditions stable or explicitly modeling them. When multiple factors change, attribute results cautiously.

Confounded changes do not identify a single cause.
keyPoints: Confounded changes do not identify a single cause.
Change the intended factor while holding other influential conditions stable or explicitly modeling them.

questions.prompt:
Different excerpts from the same document appear in both training and test sets.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Version datasets and split logic, and prevent leakage across train, validation and test partitions. Group related records when needed so near-duplicates do not cross boundaries.

Split boundaries should respect related examples.
keyPoints: Split boundaries should respect related examples.
Version datasets and split logic, and prevent leakage across train, validation and test partitions.

questions.prompt:
A rerun uses the same seed but a different preprocessing version.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Record code revision, dependencies, data version, configuration and hardware. A random seed helps but cannot replace the rest of the execution context.

Reproducibility requires the complete relevant setup.
keyPoints: Reproducibility requires the complete relevant setup.
Record code revision, dependencies, data version, configuration and hardware.

questions.prompt:
One method wins on one seed but loses on four others.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Report variability across appropriate repeated runs rather than selecting only the best seed. Distinguish variation from initialization, data sampling and evaluation uncertainty.

Single-run wins may not represent reliable improvement.
keyPoints: Single-run wins may not represent reliable improvement.
Report variability across appropriate repeated runs rather than selecting only the best seed.

questions.prompt:
A large test set finds a tiny latency improvement statistically distinguishable from zero but operationally negligible.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
An effect size describes the magnitude of a difference; an interval expresses uncertainty under its assumptions. Statistical significance alone does not establish practical usefulness.

Practical importance and statistical evidence are different questions.
keyPoints: Practical importance and statistical evidence are different questions.
An effect size describes the magnitude of a difference; an interval expresses uncertainty under its assumptions.

questions.prompt:
A team reruns released code on the original data and matches the reported score.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A reproduction often aims to recover results using the original artifacts, while an independent replication tests findings with a separately built setup; terminology varies, so state exactly what was reused.

Reports should specify reused artifacts and independent choices.
keyPoints: Reports should specify reused artifacts and independent choices.

A reproduction often aims to recover results using the original artifacts, while an independent replication tests findings with a separately built setup; terminology varies, so state exactly what was reused.

questions.prompt:
A report presents only the winning metric and omits the baseline configuration.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Structure a report around the question, method, comparison, results and limits. Keep claims proportional to evidence and provide enough detail for another researcher to inspect the experiment.

Transparent methods are necessary to assess reported results.
keyPoints: Transparent methods are necessary to assess reported results.
Structure a report around the question, method, comparison, results and limits.
